data.name: Ekaksh
data.gender_notes: Ekaksh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ekaksh is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'eka' meaning 'one' and 'aksh' meaning 'eye'. In Hindu mythology, Ekaksh is a name given to Lord Shiva when he had only one eye after the sacrifice of his second eye. This name symbolizes power, focus, and determination. The name Ekaksh carries the meaning “One-eyed, Single” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ekaksh usually hope their child will grow to embody one-eyed, single and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the single-minded focus and determination of Lord Shiva.
data.etymology: Ekaksh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One-eyed, Single.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ekaksh total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata is an ancient Sanskrit epic poem that is regarded as one of the two major sources of Hindu mythology and Indian philosophy. It is a narrative of the Kurukshetra War between the Pandava and Kaurava princes over the throne of Hastinapura. Ekaksh, also known as Karna, is one of the major characters in this epic. He is considered a hero and a tragic figure, as he is a loyal friend to Duryodhana, but ultimately fights on the side of the Pandavas.

Ekaksh, also known as Karna, is a character in various Jain and Hindu texts, including the Agni Purana. In Jain texts, he is described as a Bhagavan, a god-realized being. He is known for his devotion to Lord Shiva and is said to have attained liberation through his devotion. The Agni Purana states that Ekaksh was a sage who performed severe penance to gain the boon of having a son, who would be a great warrior and a devotee of Shiva. The son born to him was Karna.
